name: voidhormiga
description: The outreach organization's application: people, events, images and resources as tagged runes, composed into newsletters and static websites as snapping content blocks.

requires.name: voidcore
requires.note: the engine and the dispatcher; ships as libvoidcore.dll beside our binaries. The floor is 0.2.14 rather than 0.2.7 because `glyphs` (the descriptor as a host contract) and `state.glyphs` (declarations that travel with the document) are both read here, and a 0.2.13 core answers neither -- it does not fail, it returns an empty descriptor, which is the shape of failure this floor exists to refuse.

requires.name: voidmaiz
requires.note: the view and node-graph library; we are its client #2

requires.name: voidallomone
requires.note: the rules language; reached through Void Maiz's forwarding headers under the maiz:: names

requires.name: voidpalabra
requires.note: canonical encoding and the CRDT merge; compiled from source into our own target

_vendors_unversioned_note: BLAKE3, Lucide and the typefaces carry no version string in the vendored drop, so they carry none here. `mago doctor` is right that nothing can then tell whether ours is the same copy anybody else has -- but a version invented to silence a note is the wrong answer to exactly the question the field exists to ask. The fix is to record the version at the next re-vendor, when it is a fact rather than a reconstruction.
_vendors_note: The machine-readable twin of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, which stays the human index and points at the license texts, which are authoritative. Declared 2026-09-04 because `mago doctor` was right that the rule was doing two jobs: 'vendor, don't depend' decided how third-party code is ACQUIRED and quietly decided it need not be WRITTEN DOWN. Only the first was a good idea -- and once this project ships an installer, `mago notices voidhormiga` is what assembles the notices for everything actually in the binary.

vendors.name: SQLite
vendors.note: the default Data holiday: state plus normalized rows, compiled as one C file. Built with SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION (no runtime extension loading, and no libdl) and SQLITE_DQS=0 (double-quoted string literals are refused rather than silently read as identifiers).

vendors.name: libsodium
vendors.note: THE ONE CRYPTO DEPENDENCY, and the ground rule is that there is never a second and never a hand-rolled primitive: the vault, the encrypted backup, the LAN pairing, the AWS SigV4 signer and the update client's checksum all bottom out here.

vendors.name: nlohmann/json
vendors.note: header-only. Deliberately kept off the include path of the translation units that would otherwise push the link past PE's 16-bit section ceiling.

vendors.name: stb
vendors.note: stb_image 2.30 (decoding an organization's photographs) and stb_image_write 1.16 (the map's PNG exports). The declared version is stb_image's, because a version has to name one file to be checkable against it.

vendors.name: BLAKE3
vendors.note: content-addresses every ingested asset. A hand port of a hash function is exactly the code where 'it compiles' means nothing -- Cloudflare keys each uploaded file by this digest, and a wrong one does not fail loudly, it stores the file under a name the manifest does not reference. Pinned against its published vectors in tests/blake3_smoke.cpp.

vendors.name: QR Code generator (Project Nayuki)
vendors.note: the Niche Tools QR generator (2026-09-13). Taken from master at commit 3c6d0b3cefb4 (2026-08-31); the newest tagged release is v1.8.0. No version is declared because the drop is a commit rather than a release, and a version invented to fill the field is the wrong answer to the question it asks - see _vendors_unversioned_note. QR encoding is Reed-Solomon plus mask scoring, exactly the code where a hand-written version produces a picture no phone reads.

vendors.name: Inter, Source Serif 4, Space Grotesk, Lato, JetBrains Mono
vendors.note: SHIPPED BESIDE THE BINARY as vendor/fonts/ -- the TTFs are the desktop UI and the map-export atlas, the woff2 subsets under web/ are embedded by @font-face in every generated site so a deployed page carries its own faces and reaches no CDN. The OFL is permissive but NOT unconditional: the files may be bundled with and sold as part of software but may not be sold on their own, and a modified version may not reuse a Reserved Font Name. That condition travels with anyone redistributing this repository and no license choice made here can change it.

vendors.name: Font Awesome Free
vendors.note: solid glyphs only, merged into the UI atlas. Every section tab, toolbar button and map marker is one of these codepoints, which is why a font path that fails resolves to a window with no icons rather than to an error.

vendors.name: Dear ImGui
vendors.note: not vendored here: it arrives inside Void Maiz's view module. Declared so a notices list assembled from this manifest describes what is actually in the binary rather than what is in this folder.

vendors.name: GLFW
vendors.note: the same: the desktop shell's window and input, reached through Void Maiz.

interacts_with.name: voidreyna
interacts_with.note: Reyna harvests civic documents and emits a dispatcher transcript; Hormiga replays it. No link, no shared binary — the seam is the transcript format, and tests/data holds a real one.

data.root: the folder holding the state document (--state sets it)

platforms_note: `platforms` is a SHIPPING RECORD - what has been built, run by a person and handed to somebody - not a claim about what compiles. Void Hormiga 0.1.0 shipped for windows-x64 on 2026-09-08 and that is the only entry this array has earned. What COMPILES is broader and is measured rather than asserted: .github/workflows/ci.yml builds the library, the CLI, the GUI and the tests on windows-latest, macos-latest and ubuntu-latest. The distinction is Void Maiz's, adopted here the day they stated it (their platforms_note, 2026-09-08), and it is load-bearing rather than pedantic - no runner has a display, so CI cannot witness a window opening, and `it ran there` for a GUI means a person watched it. The download page states all three platforms and says `no build yet` on two of the cards; this field is what that sentence is true because of. An entry moves in here when somebody has looked at a screen. linux-x64 moved in on 2026-09-15: the author ran the Linux archive on a Linux machine and built newsletters and websites, used the map and the rest of the application, and reported it working as well as on Windows (file dialogs aside, fixed the same day).
_release_note: The `release` block is what turns an update prompt from "a new version is available" into something worth reading -- Void Mago asked for it on 2026-09-04 and the update client renders every field of it. `behavior_changes` is specifically the category a version number cannot express and a dependency resolver structurally cannot see: nothing broke, no signature moved, and somebody's data is quietly different.

release.summary: seeing each other work now happens the same way everywhere - the map and the calendar included - and members exchange only what changed instead of the whole database
adds: The map and the calendar show who else is on something, which they never did before
A Networking section in Settings: what you broadcast, what you see of others, and whether files members add are downloaded automatically
Here now, in Share database: who is on the network and what each person is working in
Each workflow shows small pictures of the people who have it open, up to three and then a count. Settings turns them off
A padlock on anything that stays on this computer, so private is something you can see rather than remember
Notes and other new things get a name that another member cannot create at the same time

behavior_changes.what: MEMBERS NOW EXCHANGE ONLY WHAT CHANGED. Keeping in sync used to send the whole database each time. It now sends the difference, through Void Palabra's sync protocol, and conflicts are shown as a question with a button per side as before. Private things and the Antfarm still never leave this computer.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: Anyone sharing a database. A member still running 0.1.4 CANNOT sync with 0.1.5 - the two speak differently. Update every computer that shares a database, or they will see each other present and exchange nothing.

behavior_changes.what: PICTURES ARE FILED UNDER THEIR OWN FINGERPRINT. A picture added to the database is now named by a checksum of its contents, which is what lets another member check that the file they received is the file that was sent. Pictures already in a database keep their old names and still work.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: Nobody has to do anything. It is the groundwork for pictures travelling between members, which today they still do not.

behavior_changes.what: A DEVICE SAYS WHICH PORT TO REACH IT ON. It used to be the same number for everybody, so two copies of Hormiga on ONE computer called themselves instead of each other. Two computers were never affected.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: Anyone testing with two copies on one machine: give each database a different share port and they will find each other.

update.note: no silent updates: the user is told an update exists and chooses it. On mobile the store is the updater and this section does not apply.
